name: Badami Cave 1 (Shaivite Cave)
description: The oldest cave in Badami, carved around 550 CE out of solid red sandstone. The most celebrated masterpiece is the life-sized, eighteen-armed dancing Shiva (Nataraja) sculpted in an energetic Tandava pose displaying 81 distinct Bharatanatyam dance mudras.
key_sculptures: 18-armed Nataraja in Tandava pose
Ardhanarishwara (half Shiva, half Parvati)
Harihara (half Shiva, half Vishnu) with Ganga and Yamuna attendants
Mahishasuramardini (Durga slaying the buffalo demon)
Carved ceiling medallions of Nagaraja with five serpent hoods
location: Badami Cave Complex, Badami, Bagalkote District
source: Archaeological Survey of India & Karnataka Tourism

name: Badami Cave 2 (Vaishnavite Cave)
description: Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, reached by climbing 64 steps above Cave 1. Features monumental relief panels depicting Vishnu's cosmic incarnations: Trivikrama (Vamana) measuring the universe with one foot raised to the heavens, and Varaha (the cosmic boar) rescuing Bhudevi.
key_sculptures: Monumental Trivikrama panel
Varaha rescuing Bhudevi panel
Ceiling panels of Vishnu riding Garuda
Frieze of frolicking Ganas in various playful poses along the plinth
location: Badami Cave Complex, Badami, Bagalkote District

name: Badami Cave 3 (Maha-Vishnu Cave)
description: The largest, most ornate, and chronologically benchmarked cave in Badami. An exact Sanskrit inscription on a veranda pillar securely dates the consecration of this Vaishnava sanctuary to Saka year 500 (578 CE) by King Mangalesha during the reign of his brother Kirtivarman I. Features traces of ancient 6th-century classical fresco paintings on the ceiling.
architectural_style: Badami Chalukyan Rock-Cut Architecture with polychrome mural traces
key_sculptures: Serene seated Vishnu resting upon the coils of the cosmic serpent Adisesha (Anantasayana)
Narasimha (Man-lion incarnation) standing majestic
Harihara
Varaha
Elaborate bracket figures of celestial couples (Mithunas)
Sanskrit epigraph of Saka 500 (578 CE)
location: Badami Cave Complex, Badami, Bagalkote District
source: Archaeological Survey of India & Official Bagalkote District Portal

name: Badami Cave 4 (Jain Cave)
description: Perched at the highest tier of the cliff, carved in the late 6th to 7th century CE. It is dedicated to Jainism and showcases exquisite carvings of Tirthankaras, depicting Parshvanatha with a multi-hooded serpent umbrella, Mahavira seated on a lion throne in dhyanamudra, and Gommateshwara (Bahubali) in deep meditation entwined with climbing forest vines.
key_sculptures: Bahubali (Gommateshwara) standing in Kayotsarga pose with creeping vines on his legs
Parshvanatha with Dharanendra's multi-headed serpent hood
Mahavira seated on a simhasana in dhyanamudra
Jain Yakshas and Yakshis (including Ambika)
location: Badami Cave Complex, Badami, Bagalkote District

name: Bhoothanatha Group of Temples
description: A picturesque cluster of 7th- to 11th-century sandstone temples located at the eastern edge of Agastya Lake. During monsoons, the lake waters lap against the temple base, creating one of the most iconic and evocative heritage panoramas in southern India.
key_sculptures: Main Bhoothanatha Shiva shrine
Rock-carved reliefs of Varaha, Vishnu, and Jain figures on the boulders behind the temple
Colonnaded open pillared mandapa extending into the lake water
location: Eastern shore of Agastya Lake, Badami, Bagalkote District
source: Archaeological Survey of India & Karnataka Tourism

name: Virupaksha Temple, Pattadakal (Lokeshwara Temple)
description: The largest and most magnificent monument at Pattadakal. Built around 740 CE by Queen Lokamahadevi to commemorate the victorious military campaign of her husband, King Vikramaditya II, over the Pallavas of Kanchi. Modeled on the Kailasanatha temple of Kanchipuram, it in turn served as the architectural prototype for the monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora.
monument_type: Structural Temple Complex with Nandi Mandapa
key_sculptures: Episodes from Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Bhagavata Purana narrative relief friezes
Pillars depicting Lingodbhava, Ravananugraha, and Tripurantaka
Monolithic black stone Nandi in an ornate pavilion
Inscriptions honoring the master architect Gundan Anivaritachari with the title 'Tribhuvanachari'
location: Pattadakal Monument Complex, Badami Taluk, Bagalkote District
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre & ASI Dharwad Circle

name: Mallikarjuna Temple, Pattadakal (Trailokyeshwara Temple)
description: Built contemporaneously with the Virupaksha temple by Queen Trailokyamahadevi (the sister of Lokamahadevi) to celebrate Vikramaditya II's Kanchi campaign. Displays a four-storied Dravida vimana with a circular griva and shikhara, featuring exquisite narrative carvings of Krishna-lila and Mahabharata battles.
key_sculptures: Krishna subduing Kaliya snake
Narasimha slaying Hiranyakashipu
Friezes from the Panchatantra tales
Intricate floral scrolls and celestial dancers
location: Pattadakal Monument Complex, Badami Taluk, Bagalkote District

name: Galaganatha Temple, Pattadakal
category: UNESCO World Heritage / North Indian Shikhara
description: An outstanding example of northern Rekha-Nagara temple architecture in Pattadakal, dating to the early 8th century CE. Features a complete curvilinear shikhara (spire) crowned with an Amalaka and Kalasha, standing in direct visual dialogue with the neighbouring Dravidian-style temples.
key_sculptures: Spectacular eight-armed Shiva slaying the demon Andhaka (Andhakasuravadha)
Curvilinear Nagara Shikhara with miniature gavaksha motifs
Riverside stone plinth overlooking the Malaprabha River
location: Pattadakal Monument Complex, Badami Taluk, Bagalkote District

name: Durga Temple Complex, Aihole
description: The crowning architectural glory of Aihole, famous for its unique apsidal (horseshoe-shaped) layout known as 'Gajaprashtha' (resembling the back of an elephant). Built between the late 7th and early 8th centuries CE, it features a magnificent open pillared peristyle corridor wrapping around the sanctum.
key_sculptures: Dynamic Mahishasuramardini piercing the buffalo demon
Varaha uplifting goddess Bhudevi with gentle reverence
Ardhanarishwara
Shiva with Nandi
Sensuous Mithuna couples carved on outer corridor pillars
location: Aihole Main Complex, Hunagund Taluk, Bagalkote District
source: Archaeological Survey of India & Karnataka Tourism

name: Lad Khan Temple, Aihole
description: One of the oldest surviving structural stone temples in India, dating to around the 5th-6th century CE. Originally conceived with a design inspired by wooden assembly halls (mandapas), featuring massive square pillars, perforated stone lattice jali windows, and a raised roof pavilion.
key_sculptures: Ornate stone lattice windows admitting dappled sunlight into the sanctum
Central Nandi pavilion inside the hall
Floral emblems and Chalukyan royal boar crests on pillar brackets
location: Aihole Main Complex, Hunagund Taluk, Bagalkote District

name: Meguti Jain Temple & Ravikirti Inscription
description: Perched atop the Meguti Hill commanding panoramic views of the entire Aihole valley. The temple contains the famous 19-line Sanskrit inscription composed in classical Champu style by court poet Ravikirti in 634 CE (Saka 556), recording the genealogy of the Chalukyas, Pulakeshin II's victory over Emperor Harsha on the Narmada River, and establishing the dates of the Mahabharata War and poets Kalidasa and Bharavi.
monument_type: Dravida Style Jain Temple with Epigraph
key_sculptures: The 634 CE Ravikirti Foundation Inscription on the eastern outer wall
Jain Tirthankara relief inside sanctum
Goddess Ambika relief
Prehistoric dolmens and megalithic stone cists located just outside temple compound
location: Meguti Hill, Aihole, Hunagund Taluk, Bagalkote District
source: Archaeological Survey of India & Epigraphia Indica
